meta.title: Census 2021 barriers to work: no car, English proficiency, lone parents, bad health
meta.quality: Accredited official statistics (Census 2021, ~97% person response, estimates adjusted for non-response). LA, region and England rows are the published LA-level figures; BEDS sums the three LA counts and recomputes %.
meta.limitations: Census day 21 March 2021 fell in the third COVID-19 lockdown, which may have affected self-reported health and household arrangements (e.g. students at home). Cell-key perturbation adds small noise to every cell, so LSOA counts do not sum exactly to LA totals and small counts (<10, common for 'cannot speak English' and lone-parent cells) are unreliable. Car/van availability counts vehicles available to the household, not driving licences or individual access, and is a household (not person) measure. English proficiency is self- or householder-reported and only asked of people whose main language is not English. General health is not age-standardised, so older areas score worse (ONS TS037ASP gives age-standardised LA figures). Lone-parent count excludes lone parents in multi-family households. Measures are five years old and Luton's population in particular has grown since.
